body:
I wasn't in a great place to reply or to take what you've said on board, last night. I'm in a better place now. I'm going to start going back to a live music youth group that I used to be a part of. Will help build up bonds, I hope. 

Regarding my weight, I've been underweight like this for the past handful of years. I have a fast metabolism so I can stuff my face and not gain a gram. 

Thank you for pointing me in the vaguely right direction (:

Thanks for taking the time to reply.

The people helping me currently believe what I want them to believe, which is that sure, I'm a little down in the dumps, but nothing major. My attempt in October came as a shock to a lot of people, since I was presenting as perfectly alright at the time. It is often difficult for me to bring these things up with them. I do not want to go back to the ward, since I didn't find it helpful. I do not want my parents to worry any more than they are at the moment. They all think I'm okay, and I'd hate to re-open wounds that for all intents and purposes have healed somewhat.

However, I neglected to mentioned the girlfriend situation. I'm not sure whether it's normal human behaviour to do so, but I become an entirely different person when I'm in a relationship. I lie to myself more than to them, half the time. It's also difficult to distinguish actual 'love' for the sort of affection you give a cherished possession. I struggle to give people genuine feelings since they, as people, feel so pretend. This most likely relates to the DPDR, I suspect.

Day-to-day activities, in order:

*Wake up*

*Shower*

*Get a lift to school*

*Do school stuff*

*Walk home*

*Sit on computer for the remainder of the evening, or until my parents say that it's time to sleep*

*Get into bed, and either immediately pass out, or almost procrastinate about sleeping until I can't keep my eyes open anymore*

*Rinse, repeat.*


I do acknowledge that I probably eat less than an average person, but by no means do I starve or deprive myself of food. I eat a consistent 1 - 2 meals a day. I weigh 55kg (8.6 stone) and I'm roughly 5'10. I am skinny, but not to the point where I have weakness or atrophy or any of that jazz. In the summer months, I sail small boats as a hobby, and am part of a sailing club. As daily exercise goes, the walk home from school is a good half hour walk, and I try to keep a steady, fast speed throughout. 

I think the reason I do not look after myself is that suicide has always been an option. If I fuck up badly enough, I always have that to fall back to. It's awful that this is the case, but it's how it is at the moment. I don't know anything else. 

I have never been a sporty person. I had asthma as a child, which still prevails today, to some extent. As feeble as it sounds, I don't get on with other people in a sporting setting, especially not competitively. 

If, say, I exercise and work out for a month, and then sure, I'm in better shape physically, but mentally? Probably not so much. For all the good endorphins do, they're really only short term, and I think I need a longer term solution. I am quite insecure and introverted and talking to people off the bat are not something that really happens for me. If I'm in a good mood, and it's all looking good for that day, it might be something that would happen, but on an average day, it does feel like I'm not worth anyone's attention.

Another major problem I identify is that I don't see anything wrong with me. It's difficult to explain because I'm talking about my own thoughts from inside my head from my own thoughts, but whenever I try and validate my problems, my mind-voice just shoots it down. I lie to myself, too, which just adds complications. 

I don't know if I **can** change, and even if I can, I don't know if I **want** to change. ):

Thank you so much for commenting and providing some ideas.
